title: Sequential Exceptions: throw, error, exit & Pattern Matching try...catch
solutionExplanation: Implements check_payment using throw for domain rejections, error for type bugs, and exit for zero payment aborts, with safe_check normalizing each class distinctly.

Throws a non-local value designed to be caught by an enclosing try/catch expression.

mentalModelCheck.question: In Erlang, what happens if you write `try Expr catch Reason -> handle(Reason) end` without specifying an exception class prefix?

options.label: The expression crashes with badarith because omitting the class prefix defaults strictly to matching `throw`, failing to catch runtime errors.
options.explanation: Correct! In Erlang syntax, `catch Pattern ->` without a class prefix matches only `throw:Pattern`. Runtime bugs like `badarith` raise `error:badarith`, which will bypass the catch and crash the process.

options.label: The clause catches all throws, errors, and exits identically.
options.explanation: To catch all three classes, you must explicitly specify `Class:Reason ->`.

options.label: The compiler throws a syntax error rejecting catch clauses without class prefixes.
options.explanation: Omitting the prefix is valid syntax, but it strictly restricts matching to throws.
